transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me a little bit about what has been bothering you and what brings you in to see me today?

I'm seeking help because I've been having a really hard time remembering parts of a traumatic event that happened about two weeks ago. Ever since it happened, I've also been feeling extremely jumpy and on edge all the time. I just don't know what to do.

I understand this has been very difficult for you. To help me get a better sense of what you are experiencing, could you tell me if these symptoms have been present consistently since the event occurred, or have they been changing in intensity over these past two weeks?
Yes, they have been consistently present every single day since the event happened two weeks ago. They haven't really let up or changed in intensity, and it has been incredibly draining.

latest_inference.note: The patient's symptoms (memory gaps, hyperarousal) began two weeks ago following a traumatic event and have been consistent since. Per the DSM-5-TR, Acute Stress Disorder is the appropriate diagnosis when symptoms last between three days and one month after trauma exposure. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder is excluded at this time because the duration of symptoms has not yet reached the one-month threshold.
